title: The Little Prince, Saint-Exupéry
subject: litterature
description: A little prince from a tiny planet teaches a stranded pilot that what really matters is invisible to the eye.

hero.hook: To tame is to create ties: the fox's lesson that the whole world took to heart.

blocks.text: **The Little Prince**, published in **1943**, is the most translated French book in the world, with versions in more than **300 languages**. Behind the simple pencil line sits a meditation on the human condition, on other people, and on the search for meaning.

Written in exile during the Second World War, it is the spiritual testament of **Antoine de Saint-Exupéry**, born in **1900** and lost in **1944**. A pilot for [[Aéropostale]], the French airmail company, he looked to the innocence of childhood for a cure to the flatness of the adult world.

sections.title: Antoine de Saint-Exupéry and the making of the tale

blocks.text: In **1942**, Saint-Exupéry was living in exile in [[New York]], because France was occupied. Oddly enough, he wrote this desert story in the comfort of [[Long Island]]. It came out in the United States in **April 1943**, published by [[Reynal & Hitchcock]], an American publishing house.

blocks.caption: Antoine de Saint-Exupéry, the writer-pilot lost at sea in 1944

blocks.text: On **July 31, 1944**, his plane, a [[Lockheed P-38 Lightning]], a twin-engine reconnaissance aircraft, vanished over the Mediterranean. The wreck was only identified in the year 2000, off Marseille.
Saint-Exupéry never saw the worldwide success of his book. In the original manuscript there was no sheep inside the crate: a friend suggested hiding it, to leave room for the reader's imagination.

sections.title: The prince's journey, a satire of the modern world

blocks.text: The story opens with an engine failure in the middle of the Sahara. The narrator, a pilot in real trouble, meets a small being who comes from asteroid **B-612**. Up there you pull out the [[baobabs]], giant trees that stand for the dangers you have to tear up the moment they appear, to save your tiny planet.

blocks.caption: Saint-Exupéry's original watercolors: simple and deep at once

blocks.text: From planet to planet, the Little Prince meets obsessed grown-ups: the **King** with absolute power, the **Vain Man** with his own reflection, the **Businessman** with owning the stars on paper. Only the **Lamplighter** is spared, because he lights the world for other people, with no wish to rule anyone.

sections.title: The fox and the philosophy of taming

blocks.text: On Earth, lost among five thousand roses, the Little Prince decides his own **Rose** is ordinary. The **Fox** teaches him to **tame**: to create ties that make another being unique in the world. “You become responsible, forever, for what you have tamed.”
It is only with the heart that one can see rightly. What is essential is invisible to the eye.
blocks.attribution: Antoine de Saint-Exupéry, The Little Prince

blocks.text: The truth of a person lies in the relationship, not in the appearance. The ending, where the Little Prince accepts the snake's bite so that he can return to his planet, is still one of the most ambiguous in literature. Death, journey, or redemption? The question stays open.

sections.title: A universal book, and a memorial

blocks.text: The book works at any age: a tale for children, a critique of materialism for adults. Asteroid **46610** was given the name Bésixdouze, after [[B-612]], the little prince's address in space.

The drawing of the hat that is really a boa that has swallowed an elephant has become the emblem of imagination against narrow logic. What has been tamed survives distance and time: the fox's lesson reaches far beyond the war that produced the tale.
**The Little Prince**, written in exile shortly before Saint-Exupéry vanished in **1944**, is a universal fable about taming and responsibility, and the most widely read French book in the world.
